title: Frontier mid-tier API pricing falls below $1 per million input tokens by Q2 2027
body: The frontier-model API market just gained a fourth aggressive seller and lost its pricing cushion in the same week. Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 launch put a priced Meta Model API into public preview at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 output — below every competing flagship tier — while OpenAI's GPT-5.6 ladder positioned Terra at $2.50/$15 as GPT-5.5-class performance at roughly half the prior cost, explicitly resetting the mid-tier cost floor competitors price against. Meta's structural position makes this a durable price war rather than a promotional skirmish: it monetized AI through ads for years and can treat API margin as optional, forcing OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to defend share in the agentic-workload segment Muse Spark is squarely targeting with its MCP Atlas and JobBench tool-use scores. The prediction: by Q2 2027, at least two of the four major frontier vendors will offer a mid-tier model — GPT-5.5-class or better capability, not a small distilled tier — at under $1 per million input tokens, with output pricing compressing proportionally. The mechanism is straight competitive response — each vendor's mid-tier is the volume workhorse for summarization, automation, and agent-orchestration pipelines, and that segment is the most price-elastic; once Meta anchors expectations at $1.25 in preview, general availability and the first competitive matching round push the floor through $1.

reasoning.because: Meta priced its first external API at $1.25/M input, under every rival flagship tier, on July 9.
reasoning.given: Terra already halved mid-tier cost; Meta's ad-funded model lets it treat API margin as optional.
reasoning.so_that: Two or more frontier vendors match with mid-tier models priced under $1/M input tokens.
reasoning.landing: By Q2 2027, across at least two of OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, and Google.
reasoning.plain_language: AI companies are in a price war, so renting a strong mid-range AI model should get much cheaper within a year.

summary: Meta's priced Muse Spark API at $1.25 per million input tokens and OpenAI's cheaper Terra tier signal a mid-tier price war. Expect at least two major frontier vendors to sell GPT-5.5-class mid-tier models under $1 per million input tokens by Q2 2027, since Meta can subsidize API margin with ads.
